Modular lambda function (λ(τ)=θ[1/2,0](0,τ)4/θ[0,0](0,τ)4)

Words: 103 Articles: 1
Modular function OurBigBook.com
The nonzero even theta constants and the Jacobi abstruse identity give λ(−1/τ)=1−λ(τ) and λ(τ+1)=λ(τ)/(λ(τ)−1). It is invariant under the principal congruence subgroup of level two. This parameter puts the associated complex elliptic curve in Legendre form y2=x(x−1)(x−λ); its Klein j-invariant is 256(1−λ+λ2)3/[λ2(1−λ)2].

Universal covering by the modular lambda function (λ:H⟶C∖{0,1})

Words: 67
Modular lambda function OurBigBook.com
The modular lambda function is invariant under the projective level-two principal congruence subgroup. That group acts freely, and its quotient is the level-two modular curve. Adding its three modular cusps gives a sphere, and λ has cusp values 0,1,∞, with simple orders in exponential cusp coordinates. Therefore it identifies the quotient with the sphere minus those three points. Since the complex upper half-plane is simply connected, this is a universal covering map, with the projective level-two group as its deck transformation group.

X(Γ)=Γ\(h∪P1(Q)).

At an ordinary point it inherits a coordinate from h; at an elliptic point of stabilizer order e a coordinate is the eth power of a local disk coordinate; and at a cusp of width h a coordinate is e2πiτ/h.

Elliptic point of a modular curve

Words: 59
Modular curve OurBigBook.com
An elliptic point of a modular curve is the image of a point of the complex upper half-plane with a nontrivial stabilizer subgroup in the effective modular subgroup. For the full modular group the stabilizer subgroup orders are two and three, represented by i and e2πi/3. A local disk coordinate u upstairs descends as ue when the stabilizer subgroup order is e. The central matrices ±I are factored out before counting this order.

Modular symbol ({α,β})

Words: 121 Articles: 1
Modular curve OurBigBook.com
A modular symbol is the relative homology class of a path between two modular cusps. Oriented paths satisfy {α,β}+{β,γ}={α,γ}. Continued fractions subdivide rational-endpoint paths into unimodular edges, giving a finite presentation through Manin symbols. The Hecke operators act by finite sums of transformed paths, so their matrices can be computed by rational linear algebra.

Manin symbol ([g]={g0,g∞})

Words: 75
Modular symbol OurBigBook.com
For a finite-index modular subgroup, a Manin symbol records a coset and its associated oriented unimodular edge. Over the rationals the presentation has the relations [g]+[gS]=0 and [g]+[gST]+[g(ST)2]=0, for inversion S and translation T. They express reversing an edge and the boundary of a triangle. Integral computation also removes torsion caused by elliptic stabilizers. The boundary map sends the symbol to its terminal cusp minus its initial cusp; its kernel is absolute homology.

X0 2 modular curve (X0​(2))

Words: 90 Articles: 1
Modular curve OurBigBook.com
The compact quotient for the Gamma 0 congruence subgroup at level two has projective index three, two modular cusps of cusp widths one and two, one order-two elliptic orbit and no order-three elliptic orbit. It has genus zero. It differs from the level-two principal-congruence curve for Γ(2), which has three modular cusps.

Discriminant-ratio coordinate on X0 2 (t=Δ(τ)/Δ(2τ))

Words: 46
X0 2 modular curve OurBigBook.com
The ratio of modular discriminants has weight zero and level Γ0​(2). It has one simple pole at infinity and one simple zero at the zero modular cusp, with no zeros or poles in the half-plane. It is a spherical coordinate by the single-pole criterion for a spherical coordinate. The Klein j-invariant is (t+256)3/t2, with t(e2πi/3)=−256.

Compactified modular curve (X(Γ))

Words: 54
Modular curve OurBigBook.com
For a finite-index subgroup of the modular group, the quotient of the complex upper half-plane becomes a compact Riemann surface after adjoining its cusp classes. At an elliptic fixed point use the quotient coordinate for the finite stabilizer; at a cusp use its exponential local parameter. Weight-zero modular forms descend to holomorphic functions on this compact surface, and hence are constant by the maximum modulus principle.

Level-two modular curve (Y(2)=H/Γ(2))

Words: 33
Modular curve OurBigBook.com
The quotient H/Γ(2) is a genus-zero Riemann surface with three cusps and no elliptic Möbius transformations, hence is biholomorphic to C∖{0,1}. The integer level-two principal congruence subgroup has projective index six; reduction modulo two gives three cusp classes.

Principal congruence modular curve genus (g(X(N))=1+24N2(N−6)​∏p∣N​(1−p−2))

Words: 122 Articles: 1
Genus formula for a modular curve OurBigBook.com
For N≥3, the principal congruence subgroup has projective index μ=21​N3∏p∣N​(1−p−2), no effective elliptic stabilizers, and all cusp widths equal to N. Hence the number of cusps is μ/N, and the genus formula for a modular curve gives the displayed formula. The exceptional levels one and two both have genus zero; the full genus-zero list is N=1,2,3,4,5. Level six has genus one and every larger level has positive genus.
Elliptic and cusp ramification for principal level
Words: 59
Principal congruence modular curve genus OurBigBook.com
For N≥2, the effective principal congruence subgroup is torsion-free. Its modular curve cover of X(1) has analytic ramification indices 2,3,N above the two elliptic orbits and the modular cusp. If μ is its projective index, the numbers of points above these three values are μ/2,μ/3,μ/N. Applying the Riemann-Hurwitz formula gives 2g−2=μ(1/6−1/N). Here μ=6 for N=2 and μ=N3∏p∣N​(1−p−2)/2 for N≥3; level one is the identity cover.

Holomorphic at a cusp

Words: 122 Articles: 1
Cusp of a modular group OurBigBook.com
A modular function is holomorphic at a cusp when its expansion in the corresponding local parameter has no negative powers. It vanishes at the cusp when that expansion has zero constant term.

Cusp holomorphy under rational slash operators

Words: 90
Holomorphic at a cusp OurBigBook.com
If f is a modular form on a finite-index subgroup and γ is rational with positive determinant, then f∣k​γ is bounded near infinity. Choose σ∈SL2​(Z) with σ∞=γ∞. The matrix σ−1γ is upper triangular and sends z to Az+B with A>0. Thus the existing cusp expansion of f∣k​σ stays bounded under this substitution. Rational conjugation of finite-index modular subgroups gives a positive period for the translate, so boundedness gives a removable singularity in its cusp parameter. Apply this to γρ for every ρ∈SL2​(Z) to obtain holomorphy at every cusp of the new subgroup. Vanishing at the cusps is preserved too.

Modular form

Modular function OurBigBook.com
A modular form is a holomorphic function on the complex upper half-plane that transforms with a fixed weight under a congruence subgroup and is holomorphic at every cusp.

Weight of a modular form (k)

Words: 34
Modular form OurBigBook.com
The modular modular weight specifies the power (cz+d)k in a modular form's transformation law. Multiplication adds modular weights. At level one, the central matrix −I excludes nonzero odd-weight forms; a nebentypus character at higher level changes this condition to ψ(−1)=(−1)k.

For even nonnegative weight, the displayed dimension follows from multiplication by the modular discriminant and the constant-coefficient map. Polynomial ring of level-one modular forms (M∗​(SL2​(Z))=C[E4​,E6​])

Words: 235 Articles: 2
Dimension of level-one modular forms OurBigBook.com
Subtract the constant term of a modular form times a same-weight monomial in E4​,E6​. The remainder is a cusp form, hence divisible by the modular discriminant. Induction on weight and 1728Δ=E43​−E62​ express every form as a weighted homogeneous polynomial in these two Eisenstein series. The number of monomials of a given weight equals the dimension of level-one modular forms, so they form a basis and the graded ring has no polynomial relation.
Graded weights separate analytic polynomial relations
Words: 95
Polynomial ring of level-one modular forms OurBigBook.com
Let Pw​(E4​,E6​) be weighted homogeneous of modular weight w, and suppose ∑w​Pw​(z)=0 as a holomorphic function. Apply the modular group matrices (1n​01​). At a fixed point z in the complex upper half-plane, this gives ∑w​(nz+1)wPw​(z)=0 for every integer n. A polynomial with infinitely many roots vanishes identically, so every Pw​(z)=0. Within one modular weight, the monomials reduce to powers of E43​/E62​, after taking out a common factor. This ratio is nonconstant, as its Fourier expansion begins 1+1728q+⋯, so its powers are linearly independent. This proves algebraic independence even when the generators are regarded as analytic functions rather than elements of a formal graded ring.
Rational structure of level-one modular forms (M∗​(SL2​(Z),Q)=Q[E4​,E6​])
Words: 76
Polynomial ring of level-one modular forms OurBigBook.com
A level-one modular form with rational Fourier coefficients is a weighted homogeneous polynomial with rational coefficients in the normalized Eisenstein series E4​,E6​. Subtract its constant coefficient times a same-weight monomial. The remainder is a cusp form; divide it by Δ0​=(E43​−E62​)/1728=q+O(q2). The valence formula for the modular group shows that Δ0​ has no interior zeros, so this quotient is holomorphic and has rational coefficients. Induction on weight proves the assertion. Euler's Bernoulli number formula for even zeta values then gives the corresponding rational weighted polynomial in the unnormalized lattice Eisenstein sums G4​,G6​.

Modular forms as meromorphic differentials on X(1) (f(τ)(dτ)k∈H0(X(1),K⊗k(D)))

Words: 82
Modular form OurBigBook.com
A weight-2k modular form descends as an invariant tensor differential. At an elliptic point of order e, a local invariant coordinate is w=ue, so its descended coefficient has a pole of order at most ⌊k(e−1)/e⌋. At infinity, dτ=dq/(2πiq) gives a pole of order at most k. Thus D=k[∞]+⌊k/2⌋[i]+⌊2k/3⌋[ρ] bounds the poles. Conversely these bounds give holomorphic pullbacks. The Riemann-Roch theorem on the compactified modular curve proves finite-dimensionality; since X(1) is the Riemann sphere, the dimension is max(0,1−k+⌊k/2⌋+⌊2k/3⌋).

Integral triangular basis of level-one modular forms (Fj​=ΔjE4aj​​E6bj​​=qj+O(qj+1))

Words: 68
Modular form OurBigBook.com
Choose 4aj​+6bj​=k−12j with nonnegative exponents, for every j with k−12j≥0 and k−12j=2. The Eisenstein series and the modular discriminant give modular forms with integer coefficients and distinct first powers of q. The valence formula for the modular group shows that these form a basis. Successively subtracting their leading terms proves that integral coefficients up to the greatest such j force all coefficients to be integral. This is more precise than merely spanning by arbitrary monomials in E4​,E6​.

Modular form on a finite-index subgroup (Mk​(Γ))

Words: 178 Articles: 2
Modular form OurBigBook.com
A modular form on an arbitrary finite-index subgroup Γ≤SL2​(Z) is a holomorphic function on the complex upper half-plane, invariant under the weight-k slash operator for modular forms, and holomorphic at a cusp at every cusp of a modular group for Γ. If σ∈SL2​(Z) maps infinity to a cusp, choose a genuine translation period h>0 with σThσ−1∈Γ. Then f∣k​σ has a convergent series in e2πiz/h with nonnegative exponents. A cusp form has zero constant term at every cusp. This definition allows noncongruence subgroups and avoids sign ambiguities in odd weights when a smaller width is defined only modulo the center.

A Dirichlet character ψ modulo N specifying the displayed transformation law is the nebentypus of a modular form. The action of −I forces ψ(−1)=(−1)k for a nonzero form. It describes a character eigenspace of the diamond action rather than an additional analytic condition at modular cusps.

For a finite-index inclusion of modular groups and a form with trivial multiplier, multiply its slash operator for modular forms translates over left coset representatives. The Serre derivative sends a level-one weight-k modular form to weight k+2. Differentiating f(−1/z)=zkf(z) produces the extra term kzk+1f/(2πi); the anomalous transformation of the Eisenstein series of weight two cancels it. Translation invariance and the Fourier expansion of a modular form verify the remaining holomorphy conditions. For k>0, its constant coefficient is −ka0​(f)/12, so it is a cusp form exactly when f is.

First Rankin-Cohen bracket ([f,g]1​=ℓgDf−kfDg)

Words: 51
Serre derivative OurBigBook.com
For modular forms f,g of weights k,ℓ, respectively, the displayed combination cancels the anomaly in derivative transformation of a weak modular form and is a weight-k+ℓ+2 cusp form. Equivalently, for weights k,ℓ in the order f,g, a conventional first bracket is kfDg−ℓgDf; its negative is equally modular. Differentiation kills each constant Fourier coefficient, proving cusp vanishing.

The valence formula for the modular group shows that Δ=(E43​−E62​)/1728 has no zeros in the half-plane. For every a∈C, the weight-twelve form E43​−aΔ has total weighted zero order one. At a=0 its sole zero is the order-three zero at the cubic elliptic orbit; at a=1728 its sole zero is the order-two zero at the quadratic elliptic orbit. Otherwise it has one simple ordinary zero orbit. Thus each value of the Klein j-invariant occurs on exactly one modular orbit and classifies one homothety of complex lattices.

Modular form OurBigBook.com
A theta function is a holomorphic function formed by summing an exponential quadratic form over a lattice.

Riemann theta function (θ(z,B)=∑n∈Zg​eπintBn+2πintz)

Words: 70
Theta function OurBigBook.com
For a symmetric matrix B with positive definite imaginary part, this theta function converges normally on compact subsets of Cg. It obeys θ(z+m+Bn,B)=e−πintBn−2πintzθ(z,B), so its zeros define a divisor on the associated complex torus. If B is a curve's normalized period matrix, its zero divisor is a translate of the effective degree-g−1 locus, by the Riemann vanishing theorem. A general symmetric positive period matrix need not come from a curve.

For a full Euclidean lattice Λ and a positive definite real symmetric matrix A, the Gaussian theta sum is θΛ​(A)=∑λ∈Λ​e−πλTAλ. Its absolute convergence follows from Gaussian decay and the polynomial growth of the number of lattice points in a ball. The Poisson summation formula for a Euclidean lattice gives its anisotropic theta functional equation.

The lattice theta series of a full-rank Euclidean lattice records the multiset of squared lengths of lattice vectors. The Gaussian form shown here converges for t>0. For a flat torus Rd/Λ, its heat trace is ΘΛ∗​(4πt), by the spectrum of a flat torus. Equal theta series do not in general imply orthogonal equivalence of lattices.

If every eigenvalue of a positive definite symmetric matrix A tends to zero, then the anisotropic theta functional equation and the dominated convergence theorem show that (detA)1/2θΛ​(A)→covol(Λ)−1. Indeed all eigenvalues of A−1 tend to infinity, the zero term of the dual Gaussian theta sum is one, and its remaining terms tend to zero while being dominated by a fixed summable Gaussian. Merely requiring detA→0 is insufficient.

Theta constant (Θ[α,β](τ)=θ[α,β](0,τ))
Words: 55
Theta function with characteristics OurBigBook.com
A theta function with characteristics evaluated at spatial argument zero. Its dependence on τ∈H remains holomorphic. Among the four half-integer characteristic choices, the odd one vanishes identically, whereas the three even constants are nonzero on the half-plane. The zeros of theta functions with characteristics locate their spatial zero away from the origin. Ratios of equal powers of even constants yield the modular lambda function and other modular-invariant functions.

The numerator has simple zeros at π(1+τ)/2+πZ+πτZ, while the denominator has simple zeros at πτ/2+πZ+πτZ. The two sets are disjoint, so any period must lie in πZ+πτZ, by translating the zero set. The sign rule then gives the displayed exact lattice. Squaring the ratio removes that sign and has precisely the smaller lattice πZ+πτZ.

Let L be the set of complex lattices. A weight-k lattice function satisfies F(λΛ)=λ−kF(Λ). Evaluating at Λτ​=Zτ+Z identifies such functions with weight-k modular-invariant functions on the upper half-plane.

Words: 264 Articles: 5
Lattice model of a modular form OurBigBook.com
A Gamma 1 level structure on a complex lattice Λ is a point of exact order N in C/Λ. Similarity classes of such pairs are parametrized by Γ1​(N)\h.
Diamond operator (⟨d⟩F(L,t)=F(L,dt))
Words: 48
Gamma 1 level structure on a complex lattice OurBigBook.com
Multiplication of a marked point by a unit modulo N gives the diamond action. In modular coordinates this is the slash action of a lift in Γ0​(N) with lower-right entry d. Its Dirichlet character eigenspaces give nebentypus modular forms. For a nonzero form, the action of −1 imposes χ(−1)=(−1)k.

Words: 103 Articles: 1
Gamma 1 level structure on a complex lattice OurBigBook.com
Sum over index-p overlattices in which the marked point retains exact order N. There are p+1 summands at good primes and p at bad primes. With homogeneity F(uL,ut)=u−kF(L,t), the coefficient 1/p is the normalization giving the standard Hecke operator Fourier action. Cusp holomorphy under rational slash operators proves preservation of modular forms.

Words: 57
Hecke operator on marked lattices OurBigBook.com
At a prime not dividing the level, the root-of-unity average contributes apn​ and the scaling overlattice contributes the second term. At a prime dividing the level that overlattice loses the marked point's exact order and is excluded. Extending the Dirichlet character by zero gives a uniform formula, with an/p​=0 unless p∣n. The bad-prime operator is Up​.
